forecasts.why: Synthetic interactions give a random forest a plausible route to substantially outperform the 0.6313 baseline, but the 0.80 CV threshold is demanding with no observed pilot performance.

Multiple sibling models cleared the held-out floor with small estimate gaps, and random forests can capture interactions natively, but the still-open raw-feature CV milestone leaves meaningful uncertainty about both the AUC floor and agreement criteria.
The baseline AUC is only 0.6313, and raw 12-dimensional KNN without feature selection or constructed interactions is unlikely to gain enough from tuning k and weighting alone to reach 0.80.

The sibling KNN’s 0.8405 held-out AUC and small gap show that the floor is attainable with stable estimation, but the raw-feature route has not yet demonstrated the required 0.80 CV AUC and may lose performance on interaction-heavy data.
The baseline AUC of 0.6313 is far below the 0.80 threshold, and tuning a logistic regression on interaction-driven data is unlikely to deliver such a large first-attempt improvement.

Although all five sibling holdout runs succeeded with small gaps, their nonlinear, penalised, or interaction-aware approaches may succeed where a plain logistic regression on the raw features underfits the synthetic interactions and misses the AUC floor.
